purpose: Deliver the smallest falsifiable Harness loop on real project work, starting with recovery from this repository's own drift.

increments.observedProblem: The current machine plan predates the Harness identity, mixes research and governance evidence with product outcomes, and can remain green while the user receives no product increment.
increments.hypothesis: Replacing that authority with one finite product acceptance map and enforcing plan-to-acceptance mapping will stop artifact growth from masquerading as product progress.
increments.falsifier: The new verifier passes while an active work item is unmapped, a predecessor authority drives an active surface, or guardrails increase the product progress count.
increments.stopCondition: The current product authority is independent, the real reset task has a non-null route, targeted cleanup is recorded, the public verifier passes, and the change is committed and pushed.

increments.observedProblem: Long collaboration chains can lose the active goal, authority boundary, open work, and causal rationale.
increments.hypothesis: A repository-anchored handoff and fresh-task receiver check can preserve the bounded task contract with less user reconstruction.
increments.falsifier: A fresh receiver needs the user to restate a material goal, authority, or open-work fact already carried by the Harness.
increments.stopCondition: O4 passes on a fresh real continuation event with a receiver delta, explicit claim boundary, deterministic verification, commit, and push.

increments.observedProblem: The current capability portfolio has been optimized for subtraction without proving demand coverage, while any selected external capability can still leave activation, ownership, projection, rollback, or cleanup work with the user.
increments.hypothesis: A bounded demand taxonomy, inactive reviewed cohort, and replaceable manager adapter can add decision-relevant coverage and complete preview, apply, observe, and rollback without becoming portable-core authority.
increments.falsifier: The cohort adds no decision-relevant coverage, the slice requires dual lifecycle owners or manual state reconstruction, authority expands without approval, or rollback leaves residual projection.
increments.stopCondition: O3 passes on the already-bound portfolio coverage problem through one separately authorized live transaction with accepted task coverage and zero residual projection.

deliverables: cleanup rollback and finite cohort stop rule
provenance license security dependency maintenance overlap portability and admission review
finite cohort result and cleanup receipt
exact commit-and-path binding of the historical sparse reconciliation
retain correct or subtract decisions for its 15 partial items and six evidence clusters
covered overlap conflict unevaluated and not-applicable dispositions
decision-relevant comparison of native official reviewed-external composition and self-authored capability routes plus human control
smallest host-owned authority and lifecycle evidence adapter demanded by the selected real task
regression validator that keeps O3 fail-closed on repository-authored fixtures

increments.observedProblem: The exact evidence layer at dd5fa0e is now reproducible and satisfies O3, but an outcome-only completion calculation could call the product accepted while the program and closeout work remain active. The public README also still reported the pre-O3 state.
increments.hypothesis: Promoting O3 only with its exact two evidence paths, synchronizing the public state, and requiring program=completed plus a closed increment graph before completionState=accepted will keep plan, acceptance, and delivery state causally aligned.
increments.falsifier: O3 passes from any substitute evidence, an active program reports accepted, a completed program retains an active increment or open work, the public state contradicts the machine report, or the transition requires another lifecycle run.
increments.stopCondition: Commit and push the separately reviewed O3 transition, public state synchronization, and active-program completion guard. The increment becomes eligible to close only from that pushed transition; product acceptance still requires a completed program and closed increment graph.

increments.observedProblem: The public repository now has bounded product evidence, but its onboarding and community surface still impose unnecessary learning cost: the README lacks a shortest path and progressive reader routes, CI relies on runner-default Python, contribution verification is duplicated, Code of Conduct retains the predecessor Skill-governance identity, sponsorship links to absent QR codes, the documentation license grant is ambiguous, and GitHub discovery metadata is empty.
increments.hypothesis: A smallest progressive public interface—one shortest path, explicit Python and verification contract, reader-specific deeper routes, truthful maturity and claim boundaries, coherent community/security/rights documents, and only evidenced GitHub metadata—will make the project self-service without adding template or dependency sprawl.
increments.falsifier: The change adds files or live GitHub features without a demonstrated need, duplicates verification paths, invents release or production claims, changes account/trust boundaries, leaves broken links or stale product identity, obscures the current in-progress state, or creates new temporary residue.
increments.stopCondition: English and Chinese README surfaces provide a shortest clone-and-verify path, progressive reader routes, the bounded completion standard, and current evidence limits; CI pins one supported minimum Python version with immutable official Actions; contribution, conduct, security, sponsorship, support, and license guidance are mutually consistent; only evidenced repository topics are added; no speculative templates or homepage are added; targeted cleanup, deterministic verification, commit, and origin/main push succeed.

deliverables: coherent contribution conduct security support sponsorship and license guidance
full local verification and origin/main push
